solution:
Separating variables,
$$\frac{dy}{y(1-y)}=dx.$$
Using partial fractions, $\dfrac{1}{y(1-y)}=\dfrac1y+\dfrac1{1-y}$. Integrating,
$$\ln|y|-\ln|1-y|=x+C\quad\Rightarrow\quad \ln\frac{y}{1-y}=x+C.$$
So $\dfrac{y}{1-y}=Ae^x$. With $y(0)=\tfrac12$, the left side is $1$, so $A=1$. Hence $\dfrac{y}{1-y}=e^x$, giving
$$y=\frac{e^x}{1+e^x}.$$
hints: Integrate to get ln(y/(1-y)) = x + C.
Use y(0)=1/2 to find A=1, then solve for y.
